summary: Iteration 2 backend + frontend verification PASSED. Backend: 28/28 pytest cases passing (16 previously existing + 12 new for streak, PATCH /api/tasks/{id} with snooze, and POST /api/tasks/reorder). All requested scenarios verified: streak requires auth (401), invalid date returns 400, zero-state returns {streak:0, today_completed:false}, three consecutive completions yield streak=3+today_completed=true, gap on 02-14 correctly resets to streak=1 on 02-15. PATCH requires auth, updates title, rejects date on recurring (400), and snooze flow (02-15 -> 02-16) correctly moves task visibility between dates. Reorder requires auth, persists explicit sort_index, and new tasks naturally get ascending sort_index in creation order. All existing endpoints (auth, tasks CRUD, complete/uncomplete, CORS, daily-content cache+LLM) still pass. Frontend (mobile viewport 375x667): login-screen + login-google-button render, unauthenticated root navigation redirects to /login, zero page errors, only the pre-existing 'shadow*' deprecation warning surfaces in console.

react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing: deprecated 'shadow*' style props still emit console warning ('shadow*' style props are deprecated. Use 'boxShadow'). Carried over from iteration_1. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/tasks.tsx:414-417.

action_items: Cosmetic only (no functional break): migrate 'shadow*' style props in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/tasks.tsx to 'boxShadow' to silence React Native web deprecation warning.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/streak implementation is correct: validates ISO date (raises 400 on parse error), uses Mongo aggregate to collect distinct completion days, walks backward day-by-day until first gap. O(streak) loop is bounded and safe.

PATCH /api/tasks/{id}: correctly enforces ownership via {id, user_id} filter, returns 404 if not owned/missing, rejects empty title (400), and refuses date updates on recurring tasks (400). Pydantic TaskPatch makes all fields optional so partial updates work.

POST /api/tasks/reorder: scoped per-user via user_id filter in each update_one — cannot reorder another user's tasks. Loop is fine for typical list sizes; could be batched with bulk_write for perf if lists ever grow large (non-blocking suggestion).

create_task now assigns sort_index = max(sort_index) + 1 per user; new tasks land at the end. GET /api/tasks sorts by sort_index asc, then created_at — stable ordering preserved. Older docs without sort_index will sort first (None < ints in Mongo), which is the desired backwards-compat behavior.
All endpoints stay async, exclude Mongo _id via projection, derive URLs/keys from env vars, and validate via Pydantic — consistent with established patterns.
